headline: High: shared broad egress and overlapping file/API surfaces create leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks; no direct pairwise evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and integrations, while Dexter uses autonomous execution and file scratchpads. If Chatwoot content is forwarded into Dexter without sanitization, prompt-like text could steer Dexter. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversation content is copied into Dexter prompts or scratchpads
IF Dexter treats imported text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separator before any transfer
Strip tool directives from Chatwoot exports before Dexter reads them
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like strings
Disable automatic ingestion of raw conversation text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders; Dexter handles financial data and broad API keys with broad network egress. If either side shares workspace or exports raw context, sensitive customer or financial data can leave the boundary. Because both agents have broad egress and the pairwise path is plausible, severity is high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records into Dexter inputs
IF Dexter sends imported context to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or LangSmith
IF both agents share a filesystem or operator account
mitigations: Restrict shared folders to redacted exports only
Rotate any exposed API keys before first run
Block raw customer fields from Dexter inputs
Verify outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations; Dexter has autonomous execution, multiple instances, and a scratchpad directory. Overlapping write-like effects can collide on shared resources or external services even without explicit filesystem write claims. The conflict is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same external account or dataset
IF Dexter runs multiple instances against the same scratchpad or API target
IF Chatwoot integrations and Dexter actions target the same downstream service
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or API keys per agent
Use distinct scratchpad directories per instance
Pause one agent during writes to shared services
Check for duplicate writes in a short test run
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing content and operational records; Dexter is autonomous and can act through APIs and third-party tools. If Dexter consumes Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into external actions. The downstream action-taking authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Dexter uses Chatwoot summaries or tickets as direct task inputs
IF Dexter executes actions without a human verification step
IF Chatwoot content contains stale or incomplete customer facts
mitigations: Require human approval before Dexter acts on Chatwoot-derived text
Add a verification checklist for every transferred task
Limit Dexter to read-only analysis of Chatwoot outputs
Sample one end-to-end task for incorrect propagation
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and interaction history, while Dexter touches financial data and uses multiple third-party APIs plus LangSmith. That creates a likely retention and residency mismatch risk if customer records or financial artifacts are routed through external services. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so I cannot raise to high, but the compliance gap is still material.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is sent to Dexter's third-party APIs
IF financial or market data is logged in LangSmith or external telemetry
IF retention policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Minimize fields sent from Chatwoot to Dexter
Disable or review telemetry retention settings
Confirm data-processing terms for each external API
Delete any test records after validation
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
